messages:
Maria Chen: quick heads-up — tail test on canary shows p99 jump when GPU util >78% after kernel flip
Josh Patel: can you paste the profile? is it KV misses or kernel overhead?
Maria Chen: looks like a mix: KV miss rate up, kernel-selection latency spikes, microbatching doesn't hide it :thinking:
Maria Chen: snippet from perf-tool:
```
p99: 320ms -> 780ms @ util 82%
kvmiss-rate: 14% -> 48%
kernel-switch: 1.8ms -> 12.4ms
config: microbatch=4, batch-window=10ms
```
Teju Rao: hmm microbatch=4 is small — but kernel-switch cost kills short requests. two levers: raise microbatch or soft-admit to keep headroom
Lina Gomez: what about probe-based admission? send low-freq probe to detect kernel-change transition and pre-warm KV for hot keys
Maria Chen: tried pre-warm for top-5 keys — p99 improved ~20% but throughput dropped ~8% due to headroom
Josh Patel: tradeoff as expected. need formal numbers — what's SLA p95/p99 targets?
Maria Chen: p95 target 150ms, p99 400ms
perf-bot: [automated] benchmark run 2026-03-10: batchsize=4 util=82% p95=140ms p99=780ms throughput=12rps/gpu
Teju Rao: proposal: implement soft-admit with adaptive headroom at 75% util, microbatch=6, KV prefetch for hot keys, fallback kernel nostore
Lina Gomez: also suggest kernel-switch hysteresis: require sustained condition for 200ms before swapping
Josh Patel: sounds good. can we simulate cost? higher headroom => lower rps/gpu. need model
Maria Chen: I can run sims. rough numbers: headroom 75% => throughput -12% but p99 drops to ~360ms
Teju Rao: schedule quick A/B canary for next week? add metrics: tail latency, rps, cost-per-1M tokens
Maria Chen: yeah I'll open PR with flags and perf harness. tagging @ops-bot for canary window
ops-bot: @Maria Chen canary slot requested for 2026-03-15 02:00-04:00 UTC — approved :white_check_mark:
Lina Gomez:+1: will help with eval hooks
Josh Patel: thanks all — actionable: Maria run sims + PR, Teju implement admission logic, Lina add hysteresis & prefetch, ops schedule canary
Maria Chen: on it, will post results in this thread
